call_points.text: Annual EBITDA margin guided at 14-15%, with Q1 strength pointing to the upper end.
CDMO volume growth seen at high teens in Q2 as well, after high-teens growth in Q3, Q4 and Q1.
Zambia order of USD 25 million (about ₹240 Cr) now expected in H2FY27, with similar revenue next year.
A new Baddi oral solids facility will go live near the end of FY27; capex is still being discussed.
API cost of goods fell to about 75% from over 90% last year as non-cepha products rose.
API targeted to be monthly EBITDA positive by February-March 2027 and to contribute to profit next year.
Net worth is more than ₹3,400 Cr and the company has no debt.
**Zambia JV procurement:** committed to procure medicines worth **USD 25 million** per year from Akums for FY27 and FY28.
**European CDMO contract:** supplies expected to commence from **FY28** with commitments for at least 5 more years.
**Zambia project:** total cost estimated at **~USD 45 million**; plant operations guided to commence in FY29.
**EU certifications:** management plans to have **~5 plants** EU GMP certified by FY28 to support European market ramp-up.
**Capacity expansion:** new manufacturing lines going live in **FY27** include an Oncology line and a steroid line.

(now merged with Pure & Cure Healthcare Pvt Ltd) was assessed to be Rs. 617.76 million. The DCIT also issued a notice of demand (Demand Notice) under section 156 of the Act for tax liabilities amounting to Rs. 734.46 million. Along with the Assessment Order and the Demand Notice, the DCIT issued a notice for initiation of penalty (Penalty Notice) under section 274 read with section 270A of the Act. ALL filed a civil writ petition dated November 15, 2021 (Writ Petition) before the High Court of Punjab and Haryana (P&H HC) for quashing and grant of stay against the Assessment Order, Demand Notice and the Penalty Notice. Vide order dated March 25, 2022, the P&H HC directed that the demand raised pursuant to the Assessment Order be not acted upon. The matter is currently pending.

operating_notes.text: Income Tax Department conducted a search and seizure operation from 15 January 2025 to 21 January 2025; show cause notices under section 158BC were received after the year ended 31 March 2026.
Board recommended a final dividend of ₹1.00 and a special dividend of ₹2.00 per equity share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
Certain manufacturing sites in Haridwar (SIDCUL industrial area) experienced temporary operational disruption due to labour unrest.
First commercial supply of formulations made to Europe in FY26.
Received EU GMP certifications for Oral Solids and Oral Liquids facilities, UK MHRA approval for Rivaroxaban, and Brazil ANVISA approval for injectable plant.
Overall capacity utilization improved to 44% for FY26 driven by strong CDMO volume growth.
Trade generics vertical turned EBITDA positive during Q4 FY26, while API business continued to incur losses.
Resumed over 70% of operations at Haridwar manufacturing sites following industry-wide minimum wage labour unrest.
Resumed 100% operational capacity at Haridwar sites; 4-day partial disruption caused ~₹20 Cr in delayed supply.
Received Section 158BC IT assessment orders with ₹60.09 Cr demand on Akums and ₹73.66 Cr on subsidiary Akumentis Healthcare for block period 01.04.2018 to 12.03.2025.
New injectable facility is ramping up with utilization currently in the early teens.
CDMO capacity utilisation is around 50%, with peak potential of 55-60%.
API cost of goods fell to about 75% in Q1FY27 from over 90% last year as non-cepha products rose.
Zambia order covers 100-plus products with volumes and prices agreed with the government.

NPPA demand notice of ₹52.75 Cr (overcharging ₹18.95 Cr, penalty ₹18.95 Cr, interest ₹14.85 Cr) dated 13 Oct 2026 names Pure and Cure Healthcare as manufacturer of Lanol 1000 mg injection for marketer Hetero Healthcare.

timeline.summary: On 28 April 2026, wholly-owned subsidiary Pure and Cure Healthcare leased a 4,050 sq m industrial plot adjacent to its Haridwar manufacturing facility.
Akums Drugs reported FY26 revenue of ₹4,257 Cr and recommended a total dividend of ₹3 per share, while noting receipt of show cause notices from the Income Tax department.
Akums Drugs reported a temporary disruption of operations at certain Haridwar manufacturing sites due to labour unrest at the SIDCUL industrial area.
Akums Drugs reported Q4 FY26 operating revenue of ₹1,158 Cr with Adj PAT rising 135% YoY to ₹83 Cr, supported by strong CDMO growth.
Akums issued its Q4/FY26 investor presentation outlining USD 25 mn annual Zambia JV supply commitments and FY28 commercialization for its 200 Mn Euro European CDMO contract.
On May 16, 2026, Akums Drugs resumed over 70% of operations at its Haridwar manufacturing sites following an industry-wide labour disruption over minimum wages.
Resumed 100% operations at Haridwar sites on 18 May 2026 after a 4-day disruption that delayed ~₹20 Cr of supply.
Akums Drugs and subsidiary Akumentis Healthcare received IT assessment orders under Section 158BC totaling ₹133.75 Cr for FY19-FY25.
Akums Drugs held its Q4FY26 earnings call, guiding to ₹300 Cr capex in FY27 and starting Zambia supplies by end of Q2FY27.
Akums Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Limited schedules physical investor/analyst meet on June 8, 2026, at 09:00 AM IST at Group Grand Hyatt, Mumbai, signed by Dharamvir Malik.
On its 10 August 2026 Q1FY27 call, Akums reported revenue of ₹1,167 Cr (+13.9% YoY) and PAT of ₹101 Cr (+56.1%), led by CDMO, and guided to 14-15% annual EBITDA margins.

On 15 October 2026, Akums disclosed that its wholly owned subsidiary Pure and Cure Healthcare received an NPPA demand notice of ₹52.75 Cr dated 13 October 2026 over pricing of Lanol 1000 mg injection, with liability claimed to rest on marketer Hetero Healthcare.
